newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Changan sees lower 96 net on transport glitch.
newsitem.headline: Changan sees lower 96 net on transport glitch.

text.p: Problems with vehicle deliveries are likely to push down the 1996 net profit of Chongqing Changan Automobile Co Ltd, a company official said on Friday.
Changan's 1996 net is expected to dip to around 202 million yuan in 1996 based on international accounting standards, a company official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
In its B share prospectus issued in November 1996, Changan had forecast net profit of at least 220 million yuan for 1996, compared with 220.16 million yuan in 1995 and 192.15 million yuan in 1994.
A transport squeeze contributed to Changan's 8.2 percent drop in net profit against forecast, the company official said, adding the annual report is likely to be released early next week.
"Delivery became a bottleneck by the end of 1996," he said. "Our company is in Chongqing and many of our customers are in Beijing and Shanghai."
Chongqing is in the southwestern province of Sichuan.
A cut in Changan's car prices also dragged down profits, the official said but declined to elaborate.
Analysts said Changan slashed car prices by around five percent in late 1996 to gain a larger sedan car market share, which Changan estimated at about 19 percent by the end of 1996.
"The 1996 forecast was based on interim results, and at that time Changan had not lowered prices," a J&A Securities analyst specialising in the car industry said.
Changan's sales picked up at the beginning of 1997 and the company is expected to reap a net profit of about 245 million yuan this year, the analyst said.
The Changan official said the company is expecting better results in 1997, but noted it would not be "a huge leap".
Analysts are mixed over how Changan's share price will respond to the company's 1996 annual result expected to be issued early next week.
Trading in Changan's B shares was suspended on Friday for a shareholders' meeting and will resume on Monday, the Shenzhen Stock Exchange has said.
"Investors will be cautious and may lose confidence if the annual report does come out with the lower-than-forecast profit figure," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
"Investors will not dump shares because we expect a stable company progress," the J&A analyst said.
Shareholders met on Friday and approved a plan to issue 120 million A shares in Shenzhen in May, company officials said, adding Changan has appointed China Guotai Securities as the lead underwriter.
The car maker will use proceeds to boost production capacity of small sedans to 150,000 by the end of the year 2000 from 70,400 in 1996, an official said.
The offer requires final approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission and the price has not been fixed, company officials said.
Changan closed at HK$4.73 on Thursday.
